title: Adaptive windowed composer + KV reclamation to optimize GPU skyline for streaming chat
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: For streaming chat completions we observe bursty turn arrivals plus long tail conversations that keep KV cache slots pinned on GPU memory. Current continuous-batching strategy favors strict token-throughput, which leads to memory pressure spikes and periodic evictions that cause SLO regressions (p95 token latency spikes, increased fallback to CPU).

Goal: Design and implement an adaptive 'windowed composer' that forms microbatches using a soft-deadline and affinity score, combined with a KV reclamation policy tuned for streaming workloads. The combination should reduce peak GPU memory usage (target -18% at 99th percentile), lower p95 token latency under load, and reduce the frequency of hard KV evictions that trigger model fallback.

Approach summary:
- Windowed composition: rather than fixed microbatch windows or purely session-aware bundling, compute a short adaptive window per GPU slab that uses four signals: soft deadline (per-request latency SLO), session affinity (convo continuity score), token urgency (streaming mode vs batch mode), and recent slab fullness trend. Windows close either by soft deadline or when an affinity threshold is met. This reduces jitter for streaming while still achieving coalescing for cost.
- Affinity score: combine (recent-turn-similarity, same-session-penalty, estimated remaining-turns) into a single numeric score used to preferentially merge turns. Prefer merges that keep KV prefix locality high to improve KV cache hit rate.
- KV reclamation: introduce "slot aging + TTL-aware compaction" where cold KV fragments are compacted to host memory or compressed in-GPU when slab pressure crosses a skyline threshold. Implement predictive eviction that uses a short sequence-length predictor to avoid evicting KV for sessions likely to resume in the next N seconds.
- GPU skyline optimization: monitor per-slab memory skyline (live allocations, pinned fragments, ephemeral buffers) and trigger conservative compaction/defragmentation heuristics at the first sign of sustained growth rather than waiting for OOM triggers.

Deliverables:
1) Algorithm and config knobs implemented in runtime: adaptive_window_composer (params: max_soft_deadline_ms, affinity_threshold, min_coalesce_tokens), kv_reclamation_policy (params: slot_age_ms, compaction_target_ratio, predictive_eviction_window_s), skyline_monitor thresholds.
2) Unit and integration tests covering window closure boundary cases, affinity merges correctness, and safe KV compaction under heavy streaming load.
3) Benchmarks showing p95 token latency and GPU memory tail reduction using internal streaming scenario harness (see links).
4) Rollout plan and gradual enablement with canary + fallback to legacy microbatcher.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token latency under streaming harness decreases by at least 10% compared to legacy microbatcher at target QPS
99th percentile GPU memory per-slab reduced by >= 15% in synthetic long-tail conversations
End-to-end SLO violations due to KV evictions drop by >= 50% in the canary cluster
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and has safe fallback toggle
Automated tests and benchmark harness integrated into CI with results reproducible via project doc
decisions: Use soft-deadline default of 18ms for streaming-tenancy slabs (tunable per-customer)
Affinity score will be computed in the batch planner (not the scheduler) to avoid cross-thread synchronization costs
KV compaction will first attempt in-GPU compression before host spill to avoid IO stalls; host spill is last resort
Predictive eviction model will be a lightweight logistic estimator trained on recent session-length distribution—deployed as an inline heuristic rather than an ML service for reliability
risks: Incorrect affinity tuning could increase tail latency if dissimilar turns are merged; mitigated via canary and conservative defaults
Compaction CPU overhead could interfere with other control-plane tasks under extreme load; we will cap compaction CPU budget per slab
Predictive eviction mistakes may evict hot sessions; include telemetry to detect and rollback quickly
